scope: Delivery packaging only. No training, task confirmation, model changes, or dependency changes.
prior_attempt_note: First review attempt stopped before restoration because the partial clone lacked a promised DATA_AND_FRONTEND blob and its proxy was unavailable. Retried with explicit per-file fallback to preserved bytes only after immutable prior SHA256 verification; no prior mismatch was accepted.
limitations: The artifact-only kit restores artifacts, not every frozen source file. Forty frozen sources require normal tracked checkout files plus restored members; the two phases are recorded separately.
verify-only validates archived bytes and checks conflicting existing targets; success does not mean missing targets have been materialized.
Serial save refuses an existing target with different bytes, but matching files can have their permission mode changed during restore.

Destination resolve rejects observed parent traversal, outside absolute paths and existing outside symlinks; this is not protection against concurrent filesystem/symlink replacement between checks and writes.

The restoration is not atomic and has no rollback. Earlier files or a reconstructed archive can remain after a later verification failure. Split archive save occurs before the full reconstructed archive digest check.

Manifest input paths for archive/native parts are read directly, without the destination containment check. Treat manifests and their part paths as trusted repository data; no general untrusted-manifest sandbox is claimed.

There is no archive decompression size/quota policy, and missing TRAINING_ARCHIVES or EVIDENCE_ARCHIVES manifests are silently skipped by the script. This review explicitly supplied both and checked the expected 645 count.

Tar members must be regular files and match the manifest member set/hashes, but the restore implementation itself compares sets and does not separately forbid duplicate names. The audited real archives contain no duplicate member names.
This verifies file bytes and the two Linux ELF modes, not a portable runnable environment, external Python/OS dependencies, signatures of an untrusted index, or execution on another architecture.
